meta.title: project-ideas
meta.description: A ranked backlog of project ideas to build, ordered by career impact.
meta.intro:
Ideas are ranked by career signal value — visibility to hiring managers, technical depth, and open-source appeal. Rankings favor Rust/systems work, data engineering angles (Databricks/GCP), and projects that extend the existing [wsr](https://github.com/ectorial/wsr) / [codetwin](https://github.com/carlosferreyra/codetwin) ecosystem. To propose an idea, open an issue.

Full audit on 2026-11-06 covered the then-current 27 ranked ideas, five graveyard entries, and eight additional related repositories; GitHub evidence and relevant local checkouts were inspected. Subsequent retirement update: pyrs is deprecated/retired in favor of contributing to py2many, especially its Rust backend. The current backlog has 26 ranked ideas and six graveyard entries; remaining ideas retain their relative order. `idea` means proposed or no implementation/scaffold evidence, including README-only repository setup; `in-progress` includes implementation/scaffolds and maintained projects with remaining work; `done` means the core deliverable is shipped, not that maintenance has ended. Unavailable repositories remain unresolved rather than assumed absent. See [review evidence](REVIEW.md) for retirement evidence and historical per-idea findings, access limits, and validation scope.

projects.name: wsr
projects.career_signal: A local, Wasm-sandboxed CI runner built in Rust — directly demonstrates systems programming, sandboxing, and developer tooling depth that Big Tech infra teams look for.
projects.description: A local CI runner intended to execute GitHub Actions workflows inside explicit execution boundaries, with git-hook integration planned. The current Rust workspace has typed CLI parsing, shared types, and CLI contract tests, but all eleven operational command paths report not implemented and exit unsuccessfully. The GHA frontend and execution crates remain scaffolds; the historical v0.0.2 release does not establish a working current runner.
features: Implement workflow execution through the scheduler and sandbox scaffolds
Connect GitHub Actions workflow parsing and expressions to git-hook execution
Validate capability grants and cache behavior with real workflow fixtures

projects.name: vicode
projects.career_signal: Compile-time infrastructure validation and provider-independent resource modeling demonstrate Rust type-system depth and platform engineering design.
projects.description: A planned Rust Infrastructure-from-Code framework with an early vic CLI. Current code provides version/info commands and a Validate command that prints a mock message; no resource graph, compile-time validation, or provider drivers are implemented. The v0.0.5 release packages this early scaffold.
features: Validate resource graphs and required properties at compile time
Implement provider drivers for abstract compute, database, and storage resources
Prove the vic lifecycle on a small deployable example before adding polyglot bindings

projects.name: korvex
projects.career_signal: A zero-config Rust SDK for generating idiomatic language bindings via proc macros — directly signals deep Rust internals knowledge (macros, IR design, FFI) and positions you as an ecosystem builder in the interop space.
projects.description: An annotated-Rust binding SDK scaffold organized into SDK, CLI, adapter, core, macro, shared-type, and Python/Node/WASI crates, plus xtask. The export macro currently returns its input unchanged, the core is a placeholder, and language adapters use todo! for bridge generation. CI checks the workspace, but complete cross-language generation is not implemented.
features: Annotation-driven export with `#[korvex::export]` proc macro — no config files required
Backend-agnostic adapter model: Python (pyo3), Node.js (napi-rs), WASI (WIT + component model)
CLI for inspection, validation, and code generation; extensible via custom `BindingAdapter` trait

projects.name: wsr-cloud
projects.career_signal: A cloud backend for the in-progress wsr project would demonstrate ownership from CLI to distributed infrastructure, relevant to SRE/platform roles.
projects.description: A cloud companion to [wsr](https://github.com/ectorial/wsr) (currently in-progress) that streams CI results to a GCP-hosted dashboard in real time. Workers run on Cloud Run, results land in BigQuery, and a simple UI shows run history. Ties directly into GCP Associate Cloud Engineer cert.
features: Rust agent that POSTs structured JSON run results to a Cloud Run endpoint
Pub/Sub fan-out → BigQuery sink via Dataflow template
Minimal Next.js or static HTML dashboard reading from BigQuery

projects.name: cargo-heatmap
projects.career_signal: Rust tooling ecosystem contribution — shows deep Cargo internals knowledge and open-source instincts that Big Tech infra teams actively look for.
projects.description: A `cargo` subcommand that profiles build times per crate and renders a browser-based SVG heatmap. Helps teams find slow dependencies at a glance. Fills a real gap in the Cargo ecosystem that developers search for regularly.
features: Parse `cargo build --timings` JSON output
Render interactive SVG/HTML heatmap via a lightweight WASM renderer
CLI flags: `--open`, `--json`, `--threshold <ms>`

related.label: wsr
related.note: local CI runner — shares profiling motivation

projects.name: mcp-hub-registry
projects.career_signal: AI/MCP tooling is a hot hiring signal in 2025–2026. Maintaining a community registry positions you as an ecosystem contributor before the space matures.
projects.description: A machine-readable registry of MCP servers with a schema validator, auto-discovery via GitHub topic search, and a static site. Extends [mcp-hub](https://github.com/carlosferreyra/mcp-hub) into an authoritative community resource.
features: JSON/TOML registry schema with required fields (name, transport, auth, tools)
GitHub Actions workflow that scrapes `topic:mcp-server` repos nightly and opens PRs for new entries
Static site (Astro or plain HTML) rendered from the registry

projects.name: difflog
projects.career_signal: Pure Rust systems project with a daily-use story — exactly the kind of tool that gets GitHub stars organically and shows up in "cool Rust projects" lists.
projects.description: A CLI that records every `git diff` at commit time into a local SQLite database and lets you query your personal change history with ripgrep-style search. Think `git log --all` but for the actual lines you wrote.
features: git2-rs hook installer (`post-commit`)
Incremental diff → SQLite ingestion with FTS5 full-text index
Query CLI: `difflog search <pattern>`, `difflog stats --week`

projects.name: codetwin-lsp
projects.career_signal: Extending repository architecture visualization into the editor demonstrates tooling integration and continuity of ownership.
projects.description: A proposed editor integration for CodeTwin that surfaces repository architecture visualizations and navigation. The core now inspects Rust workspace packages and declared local dependencies and generates linked Markdown pages, but source-symbol parsing and legacy language drivers remain scaffolded. Editor source navigation still depends on meaningful symbol/location models.
features: Expose source symbols and relationships through an LSP server
Link editor locations to generated architecture visualizations
Build a VS Code client after the core produces meaningful source-symbol and location models

projects.name: delta-doctor
projects.career_signal: Directly leverages Databricks Data Engineer Associate cert. Data quality tooling is a top hiring signal for data platform roles at Big Tech.
projects.description: A CLI that runs health checks on Delta Lake tables (schema drift, partition skew, Z-order staleness, vacuum hygiene) and outputs a structured report. Think `cargo check` for Delta tables.
features: Databricks SDK–based table inspector (statistics, history, properties)
Rule engine: configurable checks in TOML
Output modes: `--json`, `--html`, GitHub Actions summary annotation

projects.name: interview-ready-cli
projects.career_signal: Meta/Google interviewers value candidates who build their own prep tooling — it shows initiative and shipping instinct. Public repo gets organic traffic from job seekers.
projects.description: A TUI-based coding interview trainer that pulls problems from a local SQLite bank, times your solution, and uses Claude to critique it with a "would this pass FAANG review?" rubric. Extends [interview-ready](https://github.com/carlosferreyra/interview-ready) from a notes repo into an interactive tool.
features: Problem bank TOML schema + seed data (LC-style problems with tags)
Ratatui TUI: problem display, timer, code editor pane
Claude API call on submit → structured feedback (correctness, time complexity, style)

projects.name: llm-prices
projects.career_signal: High organic search traffic ("LLM pricing comparison"), low build effort, and demonstrates awareness of the AI ecosystem — good conversation starter in interviews.
projects.description: A tiny GitHub repo that maintains a machine-readable JSON/YAML file of LLM model pricing (input/output tokens, context window, rate limits) updated weekly by a GitHub Actions scraper. Companion to [llm-knowledge-cutoff-dates](https://github.com/carlosferreyra/llm-knowledge-cutoff-dates).
features: Schema: provider → model → {input_price, output_price, context_window, updated_at}
GitHub Actions scraper that opens a PR when prices change
Rendered comparison table in README via a generation script

projects.name: pipewatch
projects.career_signal: Real-time systems + Rust async is a rare combo in portfolios. Demonstrates tokio proficiency and full-stack thinking without heavy frontend overhead.
projects.description: A lightweight process monitor that tails stdout/stderr of any shell pipeline and streams it live to a browser via WebSocket. Like `tail -f` with a browser UI and structured log filtering.
features: Rust binary that spawns a child process and captures its streams
WebSocket server (tokio-tungstenite) broadcasting structured log lines
Single-file htmx frontend with filter/search and ANSI color support

projects.name: awesome-uvx
projects.career_signal: Being the go-to curator for a fast-growing tool (uv) builds mindshare before the ecosystem saturates. Awesome lists consistently rank well in search.
projects.description: A maintained, data-driven catalog of Python CLI tools runnable through uvx/pipx. tools.json, contribution guidance, generated documentation, maintenance regression tests, metadata synchronization, and catalog/install-validation workflows are present. Successful catalog CI and selected install checks do not certify every listed tool across runtimes.
features: Expand verified CLI recipes and executable mappings
Strengthen package/runtime compatibility checks for contributed entries
Keep release metadata and generated documentation synchronized

projects.name: marimo-hub
projects.career_signal: Marimo is gaining traction fast. Being an early ecosystem contributor (notebook gallery, component library) creates durable visibility.
projects.description: A gallery of reusable marimo notebook templates for common data engineering patterns (ingestion, EDA, Delta Lake ops, ML feature pipelines). Each template is a runnable `.py` file with parameterized inputs.
features: Template schema: metadata frontmatter (tags, stack, runtime requirements)
GitHub Actions CI that runs each template against a mock dataset
Static gallery site rendered from template metadata

projects.name: gcp-cost-sentinel
projects.career_signal: FinOps awareness is a growing hiring criterion at Big Tech cloud teams. A working GCP cost alerting tool directly demonstrates GCP cert knowledge in practice.
projects.description: A serverless GCP Cloud Function that polls the Billing API daily, computes per-service spend deltas, and fires a Telegram or Slack alert when any service exceeds a configurable threshold. Lightweight alternative to GCP Budget Alerts for fine-grained control.
features: Cloud Function triggered by Cloud Scheduler (daily)
Billing API client: fetch yesterday's spend by service
Alert logic: configurable thresholds per service in TOML/env

projects.name: schema-drift-detector
projects.career_signal: Schema evolution is a senior data engineer topic. A working tool here signals production readiness beyond tutorials.
projects.description: A lightweight daemon that subscribes to a Kafka or Pub/Sub topic, infers the JSON schema of incoming messages, and alerts when the schema diverges from a registered baseline. Stores schema history in Delta Lake.
features: Pydantic-based schema inference from sampled messages
Schema diff engine: added/removed/type-changed fields
Alert sink: structured log, Slack webhook, or GCS file

projects.name: vicode-drivers
projects.career_signal: Provider adapters for an existing Rust infrastructure framework demonstrate extensible platform design and practical cloud integration.
projects.description: A proposed driver SDK and provider implementations for Vicode’s Infrastructure-from-Code resource graph. Replaces the obsolete VS Code plugin concept and depends on stabilizing the core graph and lifecycle contracts.
features: Define a provider-driver contract for resource validation and lifecycle operations
Implement one provider with a small compute/storage example
Add conformance fixtures before supporting additional providers

projects.name: bench-rs
projects.career_signal: Benchmarking infrastructure is critical at Big Tech. A clean benchmark harness with CI-tracked regressions is the kind of thing infra interviewers notice.
projects.description: A reusable benchmark harness template for Rust projects that tracks performance regressions across commits using criterion and renders per-benchmark trend charts in GitHub Actions PR summaries.
features: Criterion benchmark template with configurable sample sizes
GitHub Actions workflow: run benches on PR, compare to `main`, post summary
SVG trend chart generated from stored JSON results

projects.name: codetwin
projects.career_signal: Repository analysis and visualization combine language tooling, graph modeling, and developer experience.
projects.description: A repository visual-documentation CLI with a working first slice for Rust workspaces: Cargo metadata inspection of packages and declared local dependencies, plus a Markdown overview and linked crate pages. Integration tests cover meaningful models, generated links, isolated packages, and protection of user-authored files. Deeper source parsing and legacy language drivers remain scaffolded; current workspace publication and wrapper availability are not established by historical releases.
features: Extend beyond Cargo manifest metadata to real source-language analysis
Extend workspace visualizations with meaningful source symbols and relationships
Maintain fixture-backed model snapshots, architecture diffs, and generated-file safety

projects.name: awesome-bunx
projects.career_signal: Maintained ecosystem catalogs show community ownership and repeatable metadata automation.
projects.description: A maintained JavaScript/TypeScript CLI catalog, complementary to awesome-uvx. Generated tool tables and weekly npm metadata-sync commits are present; continued curation and compatibility verification remain useful work.
features: Expand verified tools and runnable recipes
Validate package-to-executable mappings
Maintain metadata synchronization and contribution checks

projects.name: awesome-cargo-install
projects.career_signal: Maintained ecosystem catalogs show community ownership and repeatable metadata automation.
projects.description: A maintained Rust CLI catalog, complementary to awesome-uvx. Generated tool tables and weekly crates.io metadata-sync commits are present; continued curation and compatibility verification remain useful work.
features: Expand verified tools and runnable recipes
Validate package-to-executable mappings
Maintain metadata synchronization and contribution checks

projects.name: rust-template
projects.career_signal: Reusable project infrastructure demonstrates engineering consistency across multiple Rust products.
projects.description: An existing cargo-generate workspace template with xtask automation, dependency/action resolution hooks, and optional CLI/CI/docs scaffolding. Generation failure-path tests and a generated-template CI workflow exist. The local checkout differs from the audited remote head; this review inspected code and CI evidence but did not freshly generate and compile a disposable project, so full scaffold conformance remains unverified.
features: Smoke-test a generated workspace
Document and verify optional capabilities
Keep downstream scaffold consumers aligned

projects.name: business-card
projects.career_signal: A shipped native CLI with multiple distribution entrypoints demonstrates packaging and delivery.
projects.description: A shipped Rust CLI business card with interactive and non-interactive modes, runtime resume metadata refresh, and an embedded offline fallback. The latest inspected GitHub release is v1.2.17 with binary/distribution assets; source tests cover resume filtering, fallback, URLs, and update behavior. cargo/uvx/bunx entrypoints are documented, but the latest sampled npm/PyPI jobs were skipped and fresh end-to-end wrapper installation was not tested in this audit.
features: Maintain wrapper distribution and release artifacts
Keep the offline resume fallback synchronized

projects.name: wasi-action-kit
projects.career_signal: A working sandboxed action library would provide a practical validation target for the wsr ecosystem.
projects.description: Proposed reusable WASI actions and a conformance fixture suite for wsr. The linked ectorial/actions repository returned authenticated 404s during this audit, so its current contents cannot be verified; the earlier LICENSE-only observation is historical evidence only. No implementation of this idea was established.
features: Build one minimal action/component
Test capability failures and deterministic outputs
Document the action contract against a real wsr execution path

projects.name: cli-catalog-validator
projects.career_signal: A shared validation tool can turn catalog maintenance into reusable developer infrastructure.
projects.description: Proposed validation tooling derived from the three existing CLI catalogs. Focus on common metadata and executable checks while preserving each package manager’s runtime behavior.
features: Validate required metadata and executable mappings
Run explicitly selected CLI smoke checks in CI
Produce a structured report for catalog contributions

projects.name: teaching-repo-auditor
projects.career_signal: Educational repository administration can become a practical API and reporting portfolio project.
projects.description: Proposed read-only course-repository audit tool inspired by FRRe-DS’s 2026 TPI template and group repositories. Organization activity establishes the setting; it does not establish personal authorship of student implementations.
features: Inventory assignment repositories and expected files
Report missing CI/configuration and stale default branches
Generate a course summary with links and explicit evidence

graveyard.name: pyrs — deprecated / retired
graveyard.reason: The standalone Python-to-Rust transpiler goal is superseded by [py2many](https://github.com/py2many/py2many). Pivot to contributing upstream, especially its Rust backend, through the verified [personal fork](https://github.com/carlosferreyra/py2many). This preserves the compiler/type-inference/ownership learning and Rust interoperability rationale without duplicating the transpiler project. The [pyrs repository](https://github.com/carlosferreyra/pyrs) is archived; its [retirement README](https://github.com/carlosferreyra/pyrs/commit/ecec859a9031f982a1a4f599636a77c9523ee788), history and [Python/Rust landscape research](https://github.com/carlosferreyra/pyrs/blob/ecee7db5f9de64b2b22f102307eb6e4842879bc3/docs/python-rust-landscape.md) remain preserved. This records contribution direction, not implemented backend work or submitted upstream contributions.
